title: Foundation model and generative AI yield 3CL protease inhibitors confirmed at sub-micromolar IC50
summary: An AI-assisted 3CL-protease inhibitor study selected 249 molecules from about five million generated candidates and evaluated 18 using free-energy perturbation. Five molecules were experimentally tested; all five inhibited the target below 1 micromolar IC50, and one inhibited more strongly than its lead. MMELON activity predictions had Pearson R=0.72 in a blind test. This summary is limited to the abstract and November 13, 2026 publication metadata; it does not establish antiviral efficacy in people.
ai_technology: MMELON biomedical foundation model with generative molecular models
organization: IBM Research; Cleveland Clinic; Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine of Case Western Reserve University

evidence.tested: Five synthesized molecules tested for 3CL-protease inhibition after computational candidate generation and filtering.
evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
evidence.ai_role: Generative models produced candidate molecules; the MMELON foundation model predicted activity and supported downselection.
